messages.subject: unused combinations in facet_grid
parts:
The facet_grid documentation seems to imply that a panel is created for every combination of factors, whether data for it exists or not.

And the example below appears to illustrate this:

tst<-data.frame(region=c("a","a","b","b","b","c"),district=c("a1","a2","b1","b2","b3","c1"),percent=c(.1,.3,.2,.25,.35,.23))
ggplot(tst,aes(district,percent))+
  geom_bar(position="dodge",alpha=.3,aes(fill=district))+
  facet_grid(region~.,scales="free",space="free")+
  coord_flip()+
  opts(legend.position="none")+
  scale_y_continuous(formatter="percent")
 
However, there's an example in the facet_grid documentation that excludes combinations with no data (every model of car has just one manufacturer):

# Free scales are particularly useful for categorical variables
qplot(cty, model, data=mpg) +
 facet_grid(manufacturer ~ ., scales = "free", space = "free")
So is it possible to exclude the panels of missing data or not? And if so, why does the first example not do so, but the second does? Thanks very much for your help.

Adam Loveland

messages.subject: Re: unused combinations in facet_grid
parts:
Adam, 

It's something to do with geom_bar().  I stripped your example down to its core and couldn't get it to work for what seemed like forever (~ 5 minutes).  The good news is that it works with geom_point(), so if you were planning on graphing your data in Dennis's favorite way (i.e. dyno-mite plot) then perhaps you could consider points with error bars? 

ggplot(data=tst,aes(x=percent, y=district, colour=region))+ 
  geom_point()+ 
  facet_grid(region~.,scales="free",space="free")

Brandon

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: unused combinations in facet_grid
parts:
Hi:

This works, but it's a vertical bar plot rather than a horizontal one. It has to do with the way that the facet_grid() is set up. Unfortunately, when you coord_flip() this, the coordinates get flipped but the faceting does not...the result is pretty ugly. That the faceting does not flip is key to the outcome.

ggplot(tst,aes(district, percent))+
  geom_bar(aes(fill = district), alpha = 0.3, position = 'dodge')+
  facet_grid(. ~ region, scales="free", space = 'free')+
 # coord_flip()+

Notice that the book example did not have a coord_flip() layer; it matters. You can use position = dodge with space = 'free' in the facet_grid() statement as long as the bar charts are in sync with the faceting variable before the coord_flip() takes place (which of course makes coord_flip() pointless...)

If you flip district and percent as follows:

ggplot(tst,aes(percent, district))+
  geom_bar(aes(fill = district), alpha = 0.3, position = 'dodge')+
  facet_grid(region ~ ., scales="free", space = 'free')+
 # coord_flip()+
  opts(legend.position="none")+
  scale_x_continuous(formatter="percent")

you'll see that the levels are correct on the vertical scale because they're in sync with the faceting variable, but geom_bar() uses the y-coordinate for the count/percent/proportion, so that's why the result looks the way it does. geom_bar() is behaving as documented.

The reason your plot does not abridge levels is because the original bar charts were not in sync with the faceting variable *before* the coord_flip(). coord_flip() will flip the x and y axes *in each panel*, but it will not flip the faceting arrangement, and that is why the vertical bar plots work in this example while the horizontal ones do not.

HTH,
Dennis

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: unused combinations in facet_grid
parts:
On Sun, Feb 20, 2011 at 4:24 PM, <Adam_L...@keybank.com> wrote:

Thank you Dennis and Brandon! Thanks for the clarification. I guess I'll use points. It does seem strange the way the bar_plot  behaves when the y-axis is designated for the categorical variable (as opposed to its behavior when coord_flip is used, faceting aside).

It's not 'strange' - it's documented behavior. Look carefully at the help page of geom_bar - its required aesthetic is *x*. Unlike base or lattice, there is no analogous option for horizontal = TRUE. The output from stat_bin - whether count, percentage or proportion - is the y, and it is numeric. That is the implementation. coord_flip() interchanges the x and y axes within a panel - it does not flip facets at the same time.

You can also use geom_segment() to connect points to a designated axis; in fact, there is an example of it at the bottom of the on-line help page for geom_segment(). The size aesthetic controls the thickness of the segment, so you can manufacture it into the equivalent of a horizontal bar plot. Using your example data,

g <- ggplot(tst, aes(x = percent, y= district)
g + geom_segment(aes(colour = district,
                     yend = district, xend = 0),
                 size = 20, alpha = 0.3) +
    theme_bw() +
    facet_grid(region ~ ., scales = 'free', space = 'free') +
    scale_x_continuous(formatter = 'percent') +
    opts(legend.position = 'none')

HTH,
Dennis
